question: Even if not a member of parliament, a minister can remain in his post for a period of ________. (RPF Constable 2018 (20/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: 1 year
3 Months
2 years
6 months
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 6 months

Explanation:
According to Article 164(4) of the Indian Constitution, a person who is not a member of Parliament can be appointed as a minister. However, he must become a member of Parliament (Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha) within 6 months of his appointment. If he fails to do so, his position as minister automatically ceases. A similar provision exists for state ministers under Article 164(4). This provision ensures representation and accountability in the parliamentary system. A minister must be a member of the legislature to be responsible for his actions. This rule maintains the democratic principle that executive power is drawn from the legislature.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Maximum period a non-member minister can hold office? → 6 months
☛ Which article governs this provision? → Article 164(4)
☛ Where is this provision for state ministers? → Article 164(4)
☛ If a minister fails to become a member within 6 months? → Office automatically ends
☛ Can the President or Governor extend this period? → No, it is constitutionally fixed
question_hi: संसद का सदस्य न होने पर भी, एक मंत्री अपने पद पर ________ अवधि तक रह सकता है। (RPF Constable 2018 (20/01/2019) Shift 1)

3 महीने
2 वर्ष
6 महीने
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है 6 महीने

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 164(4) के अनुसार, कोई व्यक्ति जो संसद का सदस्य नहीं है, उसे मंत्री नियुक्त किया जा सकता है। लेकिन उसे नियुक्ति के 6 माह के भीतर संसद (लोकसभा या राज्यसभा) का सदस्य बनना अनिवार्य है। यदि वह 6 माह में सदस्य नहीं बनता है, तो उसका मंत्री पद स्वतः समाप्त हो जाता है। इसी प्रकार का प्रावधान राज्यों में मंत्रियों के लिए अनुच्छेद 164(4) में है। यह प्रावधान संसदीय प्रणाली में जनप्रतिनिधित्व और जवाबदेही सुनिश्चित करता है। मंत्री को विधायिका का सदस्य होना आवश्यक है, अन्यथा वह अपने कार्यों के लिए उत्तरदायी नहीं हो सकता।

question: What kind of discretionary power does the President of India have? (RPF Constable 2018 (20/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: None of these
Constitutional Discretion
Legal Viveks
Situational Conscience
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Situational Conscience

Explanation:
The President of India has three types of discretionary powers: constitutional discretion, legal discretion, and situational conscience. Situational conscience is the power exercised when there is no clear provision in the constitution or law, and the President makes a decision based on specific circumstances. This discretion is mainly seen during emergency situations or when no party has a clear majority. For example, when a party claims to form a government, the President decides based on the situation. This power is inherent in provisions like Article 74 and Article 112. Constitutional discretion relates to the President's power to act without ministerial advice in certain cases, while legal discretion is used in judicial matters. The Supreme Court has recognized these three categories to define the President's role in different scenarios.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which discretionary power of the President is used during emergencies? → Situational Conscience
☛ Which article deals with constitutional discretion? → Article 74
☛ Where does the President's legal discretion apply? → In judicial matters
☛ What is an example of situational conscience? → Selecting a party to form government
☛ How many types of discretionary powers does the President have? → Three types
question_hi: भारत के राष्ट्रपति के पास किस प्रकार की विवेकाधीन शक्ति होती है? (RPF Constable 2018 (20/01/2019) Shift 1)

संवैधानिक विवेक
कानूनी विवेक
परिस्थितिजन्य विवेक
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है परिस्थितिजन्य विवेक

Explanation:
भारत के राष्ट्रपति के पास तीन प्रकार की विवेकाधीन शक्तियाँ होती हैं: संवैधानिक विवेक, कानूनी विवेक और परिस्थितिजन्य विवेक। परिस्थितिजन्य विवेक वह शक्ति है जिसका प्रयोग राष्ट्रपति तब करता है जब संविधान या कानून में कोई स्पष्ट प्रावधान न हो और वह विशेष परिस्थितियों में निर्णय लेता है। यह विवेक मुख्य रूप से राष्ट्रपति के कार्यकाल के दौरान आपातकालीन स्थितियों में देखने को मिलता है। उदाहरण के लिए, जब कोई दल सरकार बनाने का दावा करता है तो राष्ट्रपति परिस्थितियों को देखकर निर्णय लेता है। यह शक्ति अनुच्छेद 74 और अनुच्छेद 112 जैसे प्रावधानों में अंतर्निहित है। संवैधानिक विवेक मंत्रिपरिषद की सलाह मानने से संबंधित है, जबकि कानूनी विवेक न्यायिक मामलों में प्रयोग होता है।

question: Based on the recommendation of ________, fundamental duties have been added to the Constitution. (RPF Constable 2018 (20/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Narayanan Murthy Committee
Montek Singh Ahluwalia Committee
Bn Srikrishna Samiti
Sardar Swaran Singh Committee
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sardar Swaran Singh Committee

Explanation:
The Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution in 1976 through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment. This was based on the recommendations of the Sardar Swaran Singh Committee. The committee emphasized the need to establish standards of conduct for Indian citizens. Under Part IV-A, Article 51A originally included ten duties, which were later increased to eleven by the 86th Amendment (2002). These duties are non-justiciable but help in fostering a sense of responsibility among citizens.

☛ Which Article contains Fundamental Duties? → Article 51A
☛ Which committee recommended Fundamental Duties? → Sardar Swaran Singh Committee
☛ In which Part are Fundamental Duties mentioned? → Part IV-A
☛ Which duty was added by the 86th Amendment? → Right to Education (for children 6-14 years)
question_hi: ________ की सिफारिश के आधार पर, मौलिक कर्तव्यों को संविधान में जोड़ा गया था। (RPF Constable 2018 (20/01/2019) Shift 1)

question: Which constitution has been adopted in the constitution to amend the constitution and the election of members of the Rajya Sabha? (RPF Constable 2018 (20/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Canadian Constitution
South African Constitution
American Constitution
British Constitution
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is South African Constitution

Explanation:
India adopted the procedure for constitutional amendment and the method of electing Rajya Sabha members from the South African Constitution. The amendment process requires a special majority in both houses of Parliament and, in some cases, ratification by states. Rajya Sabha members are elected by the elected members of state legislative assemblies using the single transferable vote system. These features were inspired by the South African model. Among other options, the Canadian Constitution provided the federal system, the American Constitution provided fundamental rights and judicial review, and the British Constitution provided the parliamentary system.

☛ From which constitution is the Rajya Sabha election method taken? → South Africa
☛ How are Rajya Sabha members elected? → Single transferable vote
☛ Feature taken from South African Constitution? → Amendment process & Rajya Sabha election
☛ Source of federal system in Indian Constitution? → Canada
question_hi: संविधान में संशोधन करने और राज्यसभा के सदस्यों के चुनाव के लिए किस संविधान को अपनाया गया है? (RPF Constable 2018 (20/01/2019) Shift 1)

question: By what kind of majority can fundamental rights be amended? (RPF Constable 2018 (20/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Simple majority
Special majority of parliament with consent of states
Full majority
Special majority of Parliament
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Special majority of Parliament

Explanation:
Under Article 368 of the Indian Constitution, fundamental rights can be amended by a special majority of Parliament. A special majority means that at least half of the total members of the House are present and at least two-thirds of those present vote in favor. Additionally, the consent of states is not required for amending fundamental rights. This process is subject to the basic structure doctrine, as established in the Kesavananda Bharati case.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What majority is required for constitutional amendment? → Special majority
☛ How is special majority defined? → Half of total members present and two-thirds voting
☛ Is state consent needed for amending fundamental rights? → No
☛ Article 368 deals with? → Constitutional amendment
☛ Kesavananda Bharati case is related to which doctrine? → Basic structure doctrine
question_hi: किस प्रकार के बहुमत से मौलिक अधिकारों में संशोधन किया जा सकता है? (RPF Constable 2018 (20/01/2019) Shift 1)

question: Reducing penalties without changing the nature of penalties is known as ___________. (RPF Constable 2018 (20/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Departure
Penalties Forgive
Punishment
Reduction
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Penalties Forgive

Explanation:
Penalties Forgive refers to reducing penalties without changing their nature. In legal and administrative contexts, this means the offender receives a lighter punishment of the same type, such as reducing a 10-year sentence to 5 years. It differs from departure (complete forgiveness), reduction (lowering fines), and punishment (generic term). The concept is often applied by executive authorities to show leniency while maintaining the original penalty category. An example is remission of prison time. Understanding these distinctions is important for competitive exams.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Penalties Forgive → Reducing penalties without changing their nature
☛ Departure → Complete forgiveness of penalty
☛ Reduction → Lowering the amount of fine
☛ Punishment → General term for penalty
☛ Executive authorities grant clemency → Penalties Forgive often involves government officials
question_hi: दंडों की प्रकृति को बदले बिना दंडों को कम करना ___________ के रूप में जाना जाता है। (RPF Constable 2018 (20/01/2019) Shift 1)
options_hi: प्रस्थान
दंड क्षमा
दंड
कमी
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है दंड क्षमा

Explanation:
दंड क्षमा (Penalty Forgive) का अर्थ है दंडों की प्रकृति में बदलाव किए बिना उन्हें कम करना। यह एक कानूनी अवधारणा है जिसमें अपराधी को मूल दंड के बजाय हल्का दंड दिया जाता है, लेकिन दंड का स्वरूप वही रहता है। उदाहरण के लिए, यदि किसी को 10 साल की सजा है और प्रशासन इसे 5 साल कर देता है, तो यह दंड क्षमा है। इसके विपरीत, प्रस्थान (Departure) का अर्थ है पूरी तरह से दंड माफ करना, दंड न्यूनीकरण (Reduction) जुर्माना कम करना है, और दंड (Punishment) सामान्य शब्द है।

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ दंड क्षमा (Penalty Forgive) → दंड की प्रकृति बदले बिना कम करना
☛ प्रस्थान (Departure) → दंड को पूरी तरह माफ करना
☛ दंड न्यूनीकरण (Reduction) → जुर्माने की राशि कम करना

question: In relation to the Finance Bill, which can be disposed of taxation, a bill can be introduced in which house of Parliament? (RPF Constable 2018 (20/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Observatory House
Rajya Sabha
Lok Sabha
Viceroy House
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lok Sabha

Explanation:
According to Article 109 of the Indian Constitution, a Finance Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha. It is different from a Money Bill as it may contain provisions related to taxation along with other financial matters. After being passed by the Lok Sabha, the Finance Bill is sent to the Rajya Sabha for consideration, which has 14 days to make recommendations. However, the Rajya Sabha cannot reject the bill; it can only suggest amendments. The Lok Sabha may accept or reject these recommendations. This process ensures that the Lok Sabha, being directly elected by the people, retains ultimate control over taxation matters. The Finance Bill is a key instrument for implementing the government's annual budget proposals.

question: Who was given full authority over the Indian administration after the Act of 1858 for the Better Government of India?  (RPF Constable 2018 (20/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: Viceroy
Secretary of State
Governor General of India
British Crown
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is British Crown

Explanation:
The Act of 1858 for the Better Government of India ended the rule of the East India Company and transferred the administration of India directly to the British Crown. Under this act, the governance of India was now carried out in the name of the British monarch. The Secretary of State for India was designated to control Indian administration on behalf of the Crown, but the supreme authority remained with the Crown itself. The Governor General was given the title of Viceroy, acting as the Crown's representative, not an independent ruler. Thus, after the Act of 1858, full authority over Indian administration was vested in the British Crown.

question: In the politics, the "Whip" office is mentioned in what?  (RPF Constable 2018 (20/01/2019) Shift 3)

Constitution
Parliamentary Legislation
Parliamentary Tradition
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Parliamentary Tradition

Explanation:
In the Indian parliamentary system, the office of 'Whip' is not mentioned in any written document but is a part of Parliamentary Tradition. The whip is responsible for directing party members to vote according to the party line. This practice is borrowed from the British Parliament and adopted in India as a parliamentary convention. It is not mentioned in the Constitution or the Rules of Procedure of the House. The whip is an informal tool of party discipline that ensures smooth functioning of parliamentary proceedings. Violating a whip can lead to disqualification, but it is not a legal compulsion. Thus, the whip office is entirely based on Parliamentary Tradition.
